title_or_category: Clinical practice guidelines for telesurgery, 2nd Edition
reason: Guideline states required bandwidth is robot/codec-specific; calls for no large delay/significant jitter/loss; recommends network+new encode/decode processing delay within 100 ms maximum; redundancy should be tested through failure/switch/recovery.

title_or_category: Expert Consensus-Based Technical Guidelines for Remote Robotic-Assisted Surgery and Procedures
reason: Defines fundamental requirements for reliable surgical-grade networking and explicitly avoids universal numeric latency/jitter/bandwidth specifications because use cases differ.

title_or_category: Clinical Recommendations for Remote Robotic Assisted Surgery From the CRSA 2025 International Consensus Conference
reason: Consensus recommends 99.999% uptime, guaranteed bandwidth, total teleoperation latency <300 ms and ideally <200 ms, minimal/no jitter and zero/near-zero loss.

title_or_category: A Multidimensional Perspective on Network Conditions in Telesurgery
reason: Pilot in-vitro navigation study treats network state as a 4D space; worsening conditions reduced feasibility and performance; latency and packet loss were dominant and interactions were significant.

title_or_category: Tele-assessment of bandwidth limitation for remote robotics surgery
reason: At 145 Mbps available bandwidth, 3–7% packet loss and visible image degradation occurred; 120-Mbps video setting performed worse than 40/20 Mbps under that constrained condition; authors concluded ≥150 Mbps for their hinotori setup.

title_or_category: Verification of delay time and image compression thresholds for telesurgery
reason: Eight robotic surgeons tested 30/50/100/150-ms delay and 120/60/30/20/10-Mbps video; 30–50 ms were rated feasible while 100–150 ms were rated lower; compression down to 10 Mbps remained usable in that setup.

title_or_category: Maximum acceptable communication delay for the realization of telesurgery
reason: 34 participants tested 0–300 ms; performance worsened as delay increased; experienced surgeons remained comparable to less-experienced no-delay performance at ≤100 ms in this setup.

title_or_category: Effect of video lag on laparoscopic surgery: correlation between performance and usability at low latencies
reason: 15 trainees and 14 surgeons showed significant performance and usability deterioration at 105 ms added video latency; surgeons were more negatively affected.

title_or_category: Influence of network latency and bandwidth on robot-assisted laparoscopic telesurgery: A pre-clinical experiment
reason: 108 animal operations over 3000 km explored 170–320-ms total latency and bandwidth down to <1 Mbps; image clarity was adaptively reduced as bandwidth narrowed; latency increased workload more than image-clarity reduction.

title_or_category: Impact of data compression and security devices on telesurgery systems
reason: hinotori tests used 120–20 Mbps image bitrates across 1-Gbps best-effort/IOWN and 100-Mbps guaranteed links; stable operation depended on adequate headroom; security devices added ≤2 ms in tested conditions.

title_or_category: Toward safe clinical deployment of remote robotic surgery in Japan: five-year validation of the hinotori system using 5G wireless communication
reason: Summarizes >30 validations: QoS prevented packet loss/video degradation under heavy competing traffic; redundancy testing showed VPN reconnection in 5–11 s after simulated failures; Sub6 SA produced more predictable behavior than some alternatives.

title_or_category: System-level evaluation of 5G standalone communication infrastructure for robotic telesurgery
reason: 5G SA configurations achieved sub-120-ms latency with stable video in controlled tests; 4G/high-bitrate NSA produced higher latency/freezes; SA Sub6 degraded beyond heavy background traffic (>400 Mbps in the reported setup).

title_or_category: Construction of redundant communications to enhance safety against communication interruptions during robotic remote surgery
reason: Two commercial lines and redundant encoder interfaces were used; across 16 pig surgeries, 175 line switches were induced and no surgeon-detected abnormalities coincided with switching.

title_or_category: Safety and reliability of telesurgery in China: a multicenter, single-arm, phase I clinical trial
reason: 18 patients across four hospitals: mean RTT 38.38±13.25 ms, jitter 0.39±0.29 ms, encode/decode latency 20.02±0.06 ms, code rate 12.77±0.57 Mbps, display latency 21.35±3.42 ms; no frame loss.

title_or_category: Reliability of urological telesurgery compared with local surgery: multicentre randomised controlled trial
reason: 72 participants randomized; telesurgery was non-inferior to local surgery under trial conditions; telesurgery distances 1000–2800 km, mean RTT 20.1–47.5 ms and 0–1.5 lost frames per telesurgery.

title_or_category: Feasibility and Safety of Cross-Regional 5G-Enabled Remote Robot-Assisted Laparoscopic Surgery: A Retrospective Case Series of 21 Patients
reason: 21 Toumai procedures over ~3700 km: mean RTT 37.7±5.6 ms, jitter 2.2±0.5 ms, no packet loss/interruption; preset local network criteria and backup carriers were used.

title_or_category: Establishing an international clinical framework for telesurgery: the first bidirectional transatlantic procedure across a world-record distance
reason: Bidirectional procedures across >12,000 km reported mean latency ~196 ms, jitter 1 ms, packet loss 0.19%, and 100% connection uptime.

title_or_category: A New Technological Approach to Robotic Telesurgery with Starlink: Safe Telesurgery
reason: Swine lung telesurgery over ~1000 km via Starlink reported average RTT ~130 ms and brief image/operation disturbances about every five minutes, possibly related to switching/weather.

title_or_category: Real-world evaluation of low-earth-orbit satellite communication for surgical telementoring: implications for future robotic surgery
reason: One session averaged 34.4 ms latency and 2.51 Mbps, but the same setup next day reached 765-ms maximum latency and low-bitrate periods with marked quality deterioration; other configurations had intermittent freezing.

title_or_category: Feasibility and safety evaluation of remote robotic surgery under high latency conditions based on satellite communication
reason: Two human liver resections used APSTAR-6D with average end-to-end latency 632 ms and low Mbps links; specialized high-delay control enabled completion.

title_or_category: The era of telesurgery: insights from ultra-long-distance Asia to Middle East human telesurgery robotic assisted radical prostatectomy
reason: Shanghai–Kuwait Toumai case reported average RTT 181.4 ms; fiber primary with 5G/wired backups and bedside robotic-surgeon takeover capability.

title_or_category: Safety and feasibility of telerobotic cholecystectomy via a 5G network: a prospective controlled clinical trial
reason: 20 remote cases over ~70 km reported average network delay 43.4 ms, jitter 4 ms, packet loss <1%, upload 98.3 Mbps and download 213 Mbps; later synthesis reports a ~3-s signal interruption triggering robot standby.

title_or_category: Safety and feasibility of robot-assisted remote radical gastrectomy for gastric cancer based on 5G communication technology (FUTURE-04)
reason: 27 cases over 15 km reported network RTT 31.6±3.8 ms but total delay 226.2±4.4 ms, showing that network RTT is not total teleoperation latency; packet loss <0.1%.

title_or_category: Telerobotic partial nephrectomy and radical prostatectomy using a hybrid network: A single-center prospective experience
reason: 13 cases over ~25 km reported median latency 12 ms over fiber and 46 ms over 5G with no major network disruptions.

title_or_category: Application of 5G Remote Robotic-assisted Laparoscopy in Urological Surgery: A Small Sample Analysis
reason: 14 cases over 52 km reported 0% packet loss, 216.5 Mbps down/86.6 Mbps up, and study-defined minimum/maximum latency measures.

title_or_category: RTP: A Transport Protocol for Real-Time Applications (RFC 3550)
reason: Defines RTP interarrival jitter from packet spacing relative to RTP timestamps and distinguishes transient congestion/jitter from persistent loss indicators.

title_or_category: RTP Payload Format for H.264 Video (RFC 6184)
reason: A lost fragment can invalidate the remaining fragments of the same NAL unit; loss therefore does not map one-to-one to a dropped video frame.

title_or_category: RTP Payload Format for High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) (RFC 7798)
reason: Requires congestion responsiveness; real-time encoders can adapt bitrate via quantization, while scalable streams may drop enhancement-layer NAL units.

title_or_category: RTP Retransmission Payload Format (RFC 4588)
reason: Retransmission can recover selected lost media packets but consumes bandwidth and time; it is useful only when retransmitted data can arrive before its playout deadline.

title_or_category: WebRTC Forward Error Correction Requirements (RFC 8854)
reason: FEC proactively spends bandwidth; RTX/FEC retransmission is preferred when RTT fits the latency budget, while proactive FEC may be useful when waiting a round trip is too slow.

title_or_category: Congestion Control Requirements for Interactive Real-Time Media (RFC 8836)
reason: Interactive media needs low delay; moderate jitter can be absorbed by jitter buffers, but late real-time media may become useless.

title_or_category: Self-Clocked Rate Adaptation for Multimedia (RFC 8298)
reason: SCReAM links congestion signals, RTP queue delay and loss events to a target media bitrate, illustrating how network conditions can drive encoder-rate changes.

title_or_category: Error concealment schemes for H.264/AVC and H.265/HEVC video decoders
reason: Reviews/spans spatial, temporal and hybrid concealment strategies showing that decoded output after packet loss depends on concealment, not just loss rate.

title_or_category: A study of packet loss effects on H.264 video quality
reason: Shows packet-loss impact depends on coding/bitrate and video-quality measurement; lower bitrate can sometimes trade source quality for improved loss resilience.

title_or_category: On the Robustness of Temporal Vision-Language Models for Surgical Endoscopy Videos
reason: Endo-C6 includes packet-loss bursts alongside defocus, haze, motion blur, shot noise and cautery smoke for temporal surgical/endoscopy VLM evaluation.

title_or_category: Generic telemedicine/video-conferencing latency papers
reason: No surgical robot/control or downstream surgical-video relevance.

title_or_category: Manufacturer marketing latency claims without independent validation
reason: Retain only when needed to describe a deployment and label as manufacturer-reported.

title_or_category: Pure cybersecurity attack literature
reason: Security architecture matters, but attack/defence research is not the main P0.6 network→video question.

title_or_category: Autonomous surgical-robot networking papers without remote human teleoperation
reason: Different control/safety regime.

title_or_category: Wireless networking simulations with no surgical system
reason: Useful engineering background but weak direct evidence.

title_or_category: Generic ImageNet/video-streaming robustness papers
reason: May inform codec mechanism but are not direct surgical evidence.

title_or_category: AI papers using frame drop without networking rationale
reason: Do not call these network-induced without mechanistic support.

title_or_category: Old telesurgery reviews that only repeat historical thresholds
reason: Prefer primary experiments and current guidelines.

title_or_category: Pure haptic-delay control papers without video/AI relevance
reason: Control implications recorded only where they shape network thresholds.

title_or_category: Satellite publicity reports without methods/telemetry
reason: Use peer-reviewed satellite evidence or clearly labelled manufacturer claims.

title_or_category: Single metric “ping” reports without delay-definition clarity
reason: RTT, one-way, added, display and total delay must remain separate.

title_or_category: Codec claims without identified transport/encoder/decoder layer
reason: Mechanism must be traceable before inclusion in experimental mapping.
